title: The sunlight on clouds that nearly started a nuclear war
hook: Sunlight on clouds almost started a nuclear war.
summary: In 1983 a Soviet satellite warning system mistook sunlight on clouds for US missiles, and officer Stanislav Petrov judged it a false alarm.
sources: Wikipedia: 1983 Soviet nuclear false alarm incident (26 Sept 1983, Oko system, Serpukhov-15, five missiles reported, sunlight on high-altitude clouds)
Wikipedia: Stanislav Petrov (lieutenant colonel, judged the alarm false, died 2017; incident became public in the 1990s)
BBC News: Stanislav Petrov, the man who may have saved the world

lines.text: Sunlight on clouds almost started a nuclear war.
In nineteen eighty-three, Soviet officer Stanislav Petrov was on night duty near Moscow.
Suddenly the alarms went off. Satellites reported American missiles heading in.
His orders were to report it, which could mean a counterattack.
But he reasoned a real attack would be bigger, and radar showed nothing.
lines.caps: But a real *attack | would be *bigger, | and *radar | showed *nothing

lines.text: He called it a false alarm, and he was right.
lines.caps: He *called it | a *false alarm, | and he was *right

lines.text: The satellites had mistaken sunlight reflecting off high clouds for rockets.

post.caption:
A machine saw missiles. One man saw a mistake.
Would you have trusted your gut over the computer?
